12.0.0.en: 1 The burden of the word of the LORD for Israel, saith the LORD, which stretcheth forth the heavens, and layeth the foundation of the earth, and formeth the spirit of man within him. 2 "Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling unto all the people round about, when they shall be in the siege both against Judah and against Jerusalem. 3 And in that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, though all the people of the earth be gathered together against it."

12.0.1.en: When the soul receives its Christ within it, the new Jerusalem becomes a member of the house of Judah, and in proportion to the graces it receives it meets resistance from the enemy (the nations), by God's permission, so that the evil of the wicked one may fill its cup and the Lord, the Giver of victory, may be revealed in His children. Through the enemy's harassment of God's children, the others become a cup of trembling to the first, and a burdensome stone to him, and a fire that burns him, as the prophet says: "Saith the LORD, which stretcheth forth the heavens, and layeth the foundation of the earth, and formeth the spirit of man within him, Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling unto all the people round about, when they shall be in the siege both against Judah and against Jerusalem. And in that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces, though all the people of the earth be gathered together against it" [1-3].

12.0.2.en: The cup of trembling often signifies the wrath of God, when a man drinks it and loses consciousness and becomes like one in a state of reeling without balance, so that no one, not even one of his sons or daughters, is able to lead him or take him by the hand. This is as it is written in Isaiah: "Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out. There is none to guide her among all the sons whom she hath brought forth; neither is there any that taketh her by the hand of all the sons that she hath brought up" (Isa 51:17-18). And as it was said by Jeremiah: "Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it. And they shall drink, and be moved, and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them" (Jer 25:15).

12.0.3.en: So when God wishes to give these peoples (as a symbol of the devil) the cup of His wrath to drink, that they may reel, He leaves them to stretch out their hands against Judah, and they fall under the wrath of God, the full measure of their own cup.

12.0.4.en: Once again God likens His children to the lifted stone, which the wicked carry in order to throw it down and shatter it, but behold, they are cut in pieces, or crushed, beneath it.

12.1.s.en: 2. The salvation of the house of Judah:

12.1.0.en: 4 In that day, saith the LORD, I will smite every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness: and I will open mine eyes upon the house of Judah, and will smite every horse of the people with blindness. 5 And the governors of Judah shall say in their heart, The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be my strength in the LORD of hosts their God. 6 In that day will I make the governors of Judah like a lamp of fire among the wood, and like a torch of fire among the sheaves; and they shall devour all the people round about, on the right hand and on the left: and Jerusalem shall abide again in her own place, even in Jerusalem. 7 The LORD also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah. 8 In that day shall the LORD defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that stumbleth among them at that day shall be as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the LORD before them. 9 And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

12.1.1.en: "In that day, saith the LORD, I will smite every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness: and I will open mine eyes upon the house of Judah, and will smite every horse of the people with blindness" [4].

12.1.2.en: He smites the horse and its rider, who resists God's work in His children. The blow is astonishment, madness and blindness; that is, the enemy loses his peace, his balance and his insight, while the Lord opens His eyes upon the house of Judah, His Church, and becomes her leader and helper, and by Him He strikes the enemy with blindness, so that he is confused in his warfare and loses the battle.

12.1.3.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that the horse here is the demon of error, falsehood and cunning, and its riders are those who promote these erroneous teachings, full of deceit; and that the blindness that strikes it is its deprivation of the Sun of Righteousness, who gives light. He also comments on God's opening His eyes upon the house of Judah, saying: [Afterward God opens His eyes upon the house of Judah, which is the church of the living God (1 Tim 3:15), where the Savior, who came from the tribe of Judah, reigns over those who have received wisdom from God, who say: "Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee" (Gen 49:8)... Upon the house of Judah the watchful God opens His eyes, that is, His luminous, watchful powers, and they enjoy enlightenment and grace, and each one prays, saying: "Look upon me and have mercy upon me" (Ps 25:16). This gift is enjoyed by all the righteous, for "the eyes of the LORD are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry" (Ps 34:15)].

12.2.0.en: Not only is God the mystery of enlightenment to the house of Judah while He strikes the enemy with blindness, but He is also the mystery of strength to His people and the shattering of the devil, His enemy, for "the governors of Judah shall say in their heart, The inhabitants of Jerusalem shall be my strength in the LORD of hosts their God" [5].

12.3.0.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that if the Messiah is the spiritual King of His Church, then the disciples are the governors of Judah, who receive God as their God, a strength to them in their work of preaching. He gives them a divine, fiery power that burns up the sheaves of straw, for he says: "In that day will I make the governors of Judah like a lamp of fire among the wood, and like a torch of fire among the sheaves; and they shall devour all the people round about, on the right hand and on the left: and Jerusalem shall abide again in her own place, even in Jerusalem. The LORD also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah" [6-7].

12.3.1.en: Although the new Judah has been called the little flock, it carries the fire of the Holy Spirit, which destroys the satanic blows from the right (self-righteousness) and from the left (impurities and lusts), and keeps the believer steadfast like Jerusalem, able to behold peace. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Being spiritually the governors of Judah, it is fitting for them to shatter, with their luminous, fiery speech, the deep fleshly will... It was said by Isaiah: "And the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame: and it shall burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day; and shall consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body" (Isa 10:17-18), meaning that He destroys the corrupt intention as well as the corrupt deeds]. It is as though the fire of the Holy Spirit, who works in the spiritual man, burns the peoples round about, on the right hand and on the left; that is, He burns the evil intentions and deeds of the soul and the body together.

12.3.2.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that the right hand and the left here signify extremes, for the Holy Spirit burns in the believer the spirit of stinginess as He burns the spirit of extravagance.

12.4.0.en: It is wonderful that when God works by His fiery Spirit in the house of Judah, He begins with the tents of Judah [7] before saving the houses and palaces, that no one may have cause for boasting. He begins with the dwellers in tents, who are without protection, that they may not boast in their victory that they obtained salvation by their strength and their impregnable fortresses and their palaces and houses.

12.4.1.en: St. Didymus the Blind speaks of the tents of Judah that the Lord saves, saying: [These tents are the virtue of which it is said in Proverbs: "The tabernacle of the upright shall flourish" (Prov 14:11), and as the psalmist sings concerning the love that these tents inspire in him: "How amiable are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!" (Ps 83:1). How should they not be loved, when they are full of those who keep their feasts, for the voices of joy and the works of grace cannot appear in any place other than the tents of the righteous (Ps 41:5; 17:15)?!].

12.4.2.en: He also sees in the tents of Judah a symbol of the mortal, humbled body that we wear, for when it enjoys God's salvation it puts on incorruption, glory and power, and is changed from a natural body to a spiritual body (1 Cor 15:42-44).

12.5.0.en: As for the nullifying of the boasting of the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem against Judah, it points to the fall of the boasting of those who are wise in their own eyes, for the meek and the simple precede them, since God works with power in the one who feels his weakness: "He that stumbleth among them at that day (shall be) as David; and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the LORD before them" [8]. That is, the weakest of them, the one who stumbles among them, will often be like David (2 Sam 17:8; 18:3), if God Himself is before him to support him. The mystery of victory is the appearance of God from the house of David, and as St. Didymus says: [The house of David here points to Mary, for the Lord comes incarnate from her. In that day, when the divine Incarnation is accomplished, the power of God is proclaimed in the new house of Judah, while the devil and his works perish and his authority over the believer is destroyed, for he says: "And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem" [9].

12.5.1.en: St. Didymus the Blind comments: [In that day draws near, when the night of ignorance and sin comes to an end, as the Apostle says: "The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light" (Rom 13:12). In that day He destroys all the peoples who bear a spirit of war against Jerusalem; He destroys those who are strangers to the truth and to the service of God, not by destroying men but by removing evil and ungodliness... Thus our Lord and Savior came seeking our lost race and delivering us by destroying all the peoples working against Jerusalem, that is, by destroying the causes of evil and war, forbidden deeds and heretical thoughts.

12.5.2.en: In brief we say that while the Lord is angry with those who resist, so that they reel from the cup of God's wrath, the believer himself is the cup [2]. And while God opens His eyes upon His children to support them and lead them in their spiritual warfare, behold, He strikes His enemies (the devil) with blindness [4]. And while God gives Himself to His children as a mystery of strength and a consuming fire, He makes the enemies (the sins) like sheaves of straw, and they are burned [6]. And while He supports the weak among His children who stumble, He destroys the enemy in his evil.

12.5.3.en: Thus the Lord supports His children, "the house of Judah," so that they enjoy His salvation through their reliance on Him, and as St. Serenus says: [Hear what the King (God) Himself says, approving the courageous men and summoning them to the spiritual warfare (against sin), saying: "Let the weak say, I am strong; let the sufferer be a wrestler" [(Joel 2:10-11) Septuagint]. Behold, you see that none but the suffering and the weak alone are those who fight in the divine battle, the weak who truly have the weakness of the centurion (Mt 8:9)... who said: "For when I am weak, then am I strong" (2 Cor 12:9), as it was said: "For my strength is made perfect in weakness" (2 Cor 12:9)].

12.6.s.en: 3. The spirit of grace and supplications:

12.6.0.en: 10 "And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn. 11 In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon. 12 And the land shall mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart; 13 The family of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the family of Shimei apart, and their wives apart; 14 All the families that remain, every family apart, and their wives apart."

12.6.1.en: When the Lord reigns over the house of Judah, He pours out His Holy Spirit upon His Church to give her every grace and to support her in her striving until she crosses this world, and at the same time those who pierced the Lord with the spear of their sins fall under eternal judgment and are in great mourning.

12.6.2.en: "And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications" [10]. As St. Didymus the Blind says: [The spirit of grace and supplications is the Holy Spirit, the Giver of grace, who is given to us from the Father of mercies (2 Cor 3:3): "After the destruction of the nations (the devil and his works) Scripture adds that in that day to which it points He will pour upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem the spirit of grace and of supplications, for He is the Father of supplications (2 Cor 1:3) and He has the Holy Spirit. Concerning this St. Paul writes: "Because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Spirit which is given unto us" (Rom 5:5). And Solomon in the Book of Wisdom says: "And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above? For so the ways of them which lived on the earth were reformed, and men were taught the things that are pleasing unto thee" (Wis 6:14-16). The Giver of the Holy Spirit says in Isaiah: "I will give thee my spirit" and also: "I have given him my spirit" (Isa 42)... as He says: "I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 3:1). And it is understood from the words of the Apostle that the spirit of grace is the Holy Spirit, for he says: "He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?" (Heb 10:28-29)... Also the spirit of grace is the spirit of supplication (compassion), which is given from the Father of mercies (2 Cor 1:3)].

12.6.3.en: This is the fruit of the Cross, for He poured out upon the Church the Holy Spirit, the spirit of grace, who overflows with His divine graces and heavenly gifts, and the spirit of compassion, who supports and shows tenderness. But concerning those who reject salvation and aim the spear of sin, it is said of them: "And they shall look upon them whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn. In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon" [10-11].

12.6.4.en: St. Didymus the Blind says: [The Jews, the killers of Christ, suffered torments and were in mourning like one for whom a man dear to them has died, and they were filled with bitterness like one who has lost his firstborn son, for they perceived the wrath of God to the uttermost (1 Thess 2:16), so their homeland was taken from them and they were scattered over all the earth].

12.6.5.en: "There shall be a great mourning in Jerusalem"... perhaps it points to the Wailing Wall, when the Jews come from every corner of the world weeping over their condition and their dispersion!

12.6.6.en: Here he describes the mourning as the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the plain of Megiddo, that place where the Egyptians killed King Josiah with their arrows, and Jeremiah the prophet and the singing men and singing women lamented him; and there had been no sorrow so general and so intense since Israel arose as a nation as there was when the royal chariot carried his body through the streets of Jerusalem to bury it.

12.6.7.en: He reveals the bitterness of this mourning by likening it to the mourning of parents over their only son. It touches the life of every family, indeed of every individual, so every family mourns apart, and the man mourns by himself and his wife by herself, for neither of them can bear to be comforted by the other, because of the terror of what they feel. Its cause is a collective offense directed against the Lord Christ who was pierced, for he says: "And they shall look upon them whom they have pierced."

12.6.8.en: Many of the Fathers comment on this phrase concerning the meeting of the wicked with the pierced Lord on the great day of the Lord. Among their words:

12.6.9.en: * They will learn that they shall know Him whom they pierced, and they will beat their breasts... Him whom they did not know before, because He came in the humility of His Incarnation.

12.6.10.en: * At the beginning they refused to recognize Him because of the humility of His Incarnation.

12.6.11.en: Tertullian * When He comes with His angels to judge (Mt 25:31), will those who pierced Him not see Him?! They will be confused, for the time will have passed because of their refusal of profitable repentance.

12.6.12.en: * He who was judged sits as Judge; He who stood before the judgment seat and was condemned for crimes falsely charged will judge the real crimes!

12.6.13.en: * He will come in a human form that the wicked will see... They look upon Him whom they pierced, for they gaze upon the body which they struck with the spear... And God remains (as far as they are concerned) hidden in the flesh, so they do not see the divinity (in its glory) after the judgment; rather, those on His right hand see it.

12.6.14.en: * The Son alone appears to the righteous and the wicked at the judgment in the same form that He had when He suffered and rose and ascended into heaven... But when the righteous go into eternal life they see Him as He is, and not as He came to judge the living and the dead, but He appears as a reward for the living!

12.6.15.en: St. Augustine The wicked mourn when they see the Lord who bore wounds on their account, but the righteous He brings into His glories, and they enjoy what the wicked cannot behold!
